original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Price the flag-43 entry of the I - G/2 side correction (Y59 += -G[59,21]/2 X21 = -1/2 X21) at #3508's co-hosted cut, where R0 holds Y59 in the head chart [95,447,6,32,20,15] after its last update 3364 and X21 in the full chart. Build and natively validate four corrected words on R0 (target lift T, source detour S, one private-copy lifetime P, and the whole Y59 row T48), give their exact before/after bills, and prove the matching obstruction: in the class that keeps the published events and ADDs, keeps endpoint frames, may retarget or insert transports, and keeps the private register C's published lifetimes, no placement of the correction ADD at any of the 28 insertion classes costs zero added rank mass, so the strict minimum is exactly 2.
scope_change_reason: #3508 (merged) answers #3456's head-step question with R0 and leaves the I - G/2 side correction at the co-hosted chart open (its open question 2). This package answers that question for the single flag-43 entry and its target row; it cites #3508/#3456 as leave-alone priors and does not re-derive R0 or the published chronology.
bottleneck_link: Head co-hosting at the target update does not discount the side correction. The flag-43 entry needs one common chart for X21 and Y59, and in every zero-added-mass repair X21's forced frame contains X12's head 131 from event 884 on (and is full from 1708), while Y59 stays inside its final hyperplane, which excludes 131. The cheapest strict correction therefore pays +2 rank mass, the same as the end-cut detour on the published word. Only the inherited private-copy contract lowers it to +1. Neither is a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after flag 43: one entry, one target row, one cut (R0's 3525 terminal transport), four validated words and the zero-mass obstruction over all insertion classes. Do not touch flags 0, 1 or 9, the other 103 target rows, global hosting, precision or kappa.
evidence: Flag-43 entry: G[59,21]=1, so I-G/2 needs -1/2 X21 in Y59. On R0 the corrections replace R0's terminal Y59 transport at 3525. T: Y59 W6->FULL (rank 3), ADD in FULL, FULL->F59 (rank 1): +2 events, +1 ADD, +1 transport occurrence, +2 rank mass, profile H1-H2+H3 vs R0, 740 edges. S: R0's transport, then X21 FULL->F59, ADD in F59, F59->FULL: +3 events, +1 ADD, +2 transport occurrences, +2 rank mass, profile 2H1, 742 edges. P: zero C at FULL, copy X21, C FULL->F59, ADD, erase: +5 events, +1 ADD, +1 transport occurrence, +1 rank mass, profile H1, private lifetimes 8->9, 741 edges. T48: the T lift carrying all 48 off-diagonal entries of row 59: +49 events, +48 ADDs, +1 transport occurrence, +2 rank mass; Y59's final row is exactly y59 + x59. The unchanged check_native.validate() passes each coefficient-0 word (native edges incl. two newly lowered FULL<->F59 recipes, 208 adapters, 280 framed rows, 72 dirty helpers) and rejects each real word only at 'full physical boundary endpoint Y59'; exact rational replay changes only Y59's row. Obstruction: event 625 (G9 += 2 X12, head 131) and 884 (G9 -= 2 X21) force 131 into X21's frame in any monotone repair; G[59,12]=0 puts 131 outside Y59's final hyperplane; a least-lower-bound sweep blocks all 28 insertion classes (before 885 via Y59's forced head hosting: Y67/Y96; from 885 on immediately). Per-register added rank mass is even, so the strict minimum is exactly 2. The published end-cut detour also costs +2: co-host discount 0. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is the +1 private-copy route P admissible as a physical correction, or must every side-correction lifetime be reversibly uncomputed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: P is cheaper than every strict route only because the inherited private-copy contract lets C be discarded while it holds a copy of X21. If that contract is not admissible for corrections, the strict bound of +2 per corrected target applies.
open_questions.first_step: Price an uncompute of C (copy back to zero in X21's chart before the erase) and compare its rank cost with S.
open_questions.blocked_by: The native channel package labels the private-copy semantics as inherited and makes no reversibility claim.

open_questions.question: Does the X12 -> G9 -> X21 forcing pattern block a zero-mass entry for every other present-head flag and for the other off-diagonal entries of row 59?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If every target row needs +2, the end-cut invoice of 208 extra rank mass is forced for strict per-target corrections. A row with a zero-mass entry would be the first place where co-hosting buys a discount.
open_questions.first_step: Run this package's sweep() for every (target, source) pair with G[t,s] != 0 on the published word and record the first forcing source head outside the target's final hyperplane.
open_questions.blocked_by: Flags 1 and 9 are subjects of other open/deferred work; this package treats flag 43 only.

open_questions.question: Can a fused correction that changes published ADD coefficients (outside the class used here) apply the entry without added rank mass, e.g. by retuning the 3364 delivery from D17?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The obstruction keeps every published ADD. D17 already delivers X21 into Y59 at 3364 through the private C descent; changing that delivery would change other target rows too.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the span of D17/Y103 rows available in the head chart W6 during 3363-3525 and test whether -1/2 X21 lies in it modulo restored helpers.
